'''Tristen Jamal Newton''' (born April 26, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Houston Rockets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), on a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[East Carolina Pirates men's basketball|East Carolina Pirates]] and with the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]] where he won both the 2023 and 2024 national championships. Newton was selected by the [[Indiana Pacers]] with the 49th overall pick in the [[2024 NBA draft]]. He has also played for the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].

==High school career==
Newton played at [[Burges High School]] in [[El Paso, Texas]], where his team routinely traveled great distances to play top teams in the large metro areas of Texas. Newton scored 3,266 points in high school and led the state in scoring as a senior at 37.2 [[points per game]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Arruda |first=Joe |date=January 28, 2023 |title=Confidence is key for UConn point guard Tristen Newton and Dan Hurley thinks he's unlocked it |url=https://www.courant.com/2023/01/28/confidence-is-key-for-uconn-point-guard-tristen-newton-and-dan-hurley-thinks-hes-unlocked-it/ |access-date=April 2, 2023 |work=[[Hartford Courant]]}}</ref>

==College career==
Newton found success at East Carolina, entering the starting lineup as a freshman and averaging 11 points and 3.7 assists per game. He set the Pirates' program record for assists in a season by a freshman.<ref>{{cite web |date=March 8, 2020 |title=ECU hoops finishes 11th; Godwin passes LeClair |url=https://www.reflector.com/sports/ecu-hoops-finishes-th-godwin-passes-leclair/article_7fce0866-d11e-53cc-9b14-ed08a1250918.html |access-date=April 2, 2023 |work=[[Daily Reflector]]}}</ref> He improved for his next two seasons, culminating in a junior season where he averaged 17.7 points, 4.8 rebounds and 5 assists per game. He was named to the All-[[American Athletic Conference]] (AAC) second team at the close of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Newton Named To All-AAC Second Team|url=https://ecupirates.com/news/2022/3/9/mens-basketball-newton-named-to-all-aac-second-team.aspx|work=[[East Carolina Pirates]]|date=March 9, 2022|access-date=April 2, 2023}}</ref>

Following the dismissal of his coach [[Joe Dooley (basketball)|Joe Dooley]] after the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]], Newton decided to transfer from East Carolina.<ref>{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=April 13, 2022 |title=East Carolina transfer, second-team All-AAC guard Tristen Newton commits to UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33730114 |access-date=April 2, 2023 |website=ESPN.com}}</ref> He heard from over 30 schools after putting his name in the NCAA transfer portal, ultimately choosing the [[University of Connecticut]] (UConn), where coach [[Dan Hurley]] saw his playmaking as a missing piece for his [[Big East Conference]] team. Newton earned the starting [[point guard]] role and became the second player in program history to record two [[triple-double]]s, joining [[Shabazz Napier]]. At the close of the season, Newton helped lead the Huskies to the sixth Final Four in school history and later, with a double-double, to UConn's fifth NCAA championship in [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2023]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Martinez |first=Quinton |date=April 1, 2023 |title='Ready for a stage like this': After move to UConn, Burges' Newton plays in Final Four |url=https://www.elpasotimes.com/story/sports/college/2023/04/01/after-move-to-uconn-burges-tristen-newton-final-four/70070096007/ |access-date=April 2, 2023 |work=[[El Paso Times]]}}</ref>

Newton returned to the program for the [[2023–24 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2023–24 season]] after initially declaring for the [[2023 NBA draft]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Borzello |first=Jeff |date=May 31, 2023 |title=Newton opts out of NBA draft, returns to UConn |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/37767865 |access-date=November 25, 2023 ==Professional career==
===Indiana Pacers / Mad Ants (2024–2025)===
On June 27, 2024, Newton was selected with the 49th overall pick by the [[Indiana Pacers]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]<ref>{{cite web|first=Evan|last=Frank|title='One of the best transfers': NBA Draft grades for new Pacers G Tristen Newton at No. 49|url=https://www.indystar.com/story/sports/nba/pacers/2024/06/27/nba-draft-grades-2024-indiana-pacers-tristen-newton-uconn/74238815007/|website=IndyStar.com|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref> and on July 27, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with them.<ref>{{cite web|title=Indiana Pacers Sign Jackson and Newton to Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/indiana-pacers-sign-jackson-and-newton-to-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=July 27, 2024|access-date=July 27, 2024}}</ref> However, On January 1, 2025, he was waived by the Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pacers Waive Tristen Newton|url=https://www.nba.com/pacers/news/pacers-waive-tristen-newton|website=NBA.com|date=January 1, 2025|access-date=January 2, 2025}}</ref>
===Minnesota Timberwolves / Iowa Wolves (2025–2026)===
On January 3, 2025, Newton was claimed off waivers by the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]], retaining his [[two-way contract]] status.<ref>{{cite web|title=Timberwolves Awarded Tristen Newton Off Waivers|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-awarded-tristen-newton-off-waivers|website=NBA.com|date=January 3, 2025|access-date=January 3, 2025}}</ref> In three appearances for Minnesota, Newton averaged no points, 1.3 rebounds, and 0.3 assists. On October 18, Newton was waived by Minnesota after losing the final roster battle to [[Johnny Juzang]].<ref>{{cite web | title=Timberwolves Waive Four Players | website=NBA | date=2025-10-18 | url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-waive-four-players-3 | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref> On November 6, 2025, Newton was named to the [[Iowa Wolves]] opening night roster.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://iowa.gleague.nba.com/news/iowa-wolves-announce-opening-night-roster|title=Iowa Wolves Announce Opening Night Roster|website=gleague.nba.com|date=November 6, 2025|access-date=November 6, 2025}}</ref>
===Houston Rockets / Rio Grande Valley Vipers (2026)===
On January 3, 2026, Newton signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Houston Rockets]], splitting time with their [[NBA G League]] affiliate the [[Rio Grande Valley Vipers]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=DuBose |first=Ben |title=Two-way roster moves: Rockets sign Tristen Newton, waive Tyler Smith |url=https://rocketswire.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/rockets/2026/01/03/two-way-roster-moves-rockets-sign-tristen-newton-waive-tyler-smith/88009389007/ |access-date=2026-01-04 |website=Rockets Wire |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Newton's older brother, Jawaun, played college basketball for [[Evansville Purple Aces men's basketball|Evansville]] and [[Southern Illinois Salukis men's basketball|Southern Illinois]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Jawaun Newton |url=https://cyclones.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/coaches/jawaun-newton/2239 |website=Iowa State Cyclones |access-date=December 28, 2024}}</ref> He is a cousin of football players [[Aaron Jones (running back)|Aaron]] and [[Alvin Jones (American football)|Alvin Jones]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Kuhagen |first=Christopher |date=April 4, 2024 |title=Packers running back Aaron Jones was a proud cousin and one of the UConn men's basketball team's biggest supporters during its national championship run |url=https://www.jsonline.com/story/sports/nfl/packers/2023/04/04/packers-running-back-aaron-jones-uconn-basketball-fan-support-cousin-tristen-newton-ncaa-tournament/70078617007/ |access-date=December 28, 2024 |website=Milwaukee Journal Sentinel}}</ref>
